messages:
alex.ng: FYI noticed a regression in recent perf runs after infra bumped the NVIDIA driver and CUDA 12.2.2 on the dedicated pool. Short sequences (<=64) are ~20% slower for our small-batch path. attaching quick repro and profiler snippets below.

sam.k: Ugh. Which pool? Dedicated-3?

alex.ng: Dedicated-3. Repro command: 
```bash
PYTORCH_JIT=0 python perf/repro/run_inference.py --model redwood/base-7b --seq 32 --batch 4 --iters 200 --device cuda:0
```

maria.z: Has perf-ci flagged this in nightly?

perf-ci: nightly/perf-heap: regression detected on commit f8a2e3c vs baseline 1.2.3. Metric: p50 latency small-batch (seq<=64, bs=4) +22%. See graph: https://perf.internal/rdw/compare/17636

ryan.t: I pulled a quick nvprof-like trace. Kernel timing skew: previously attention_kernel_v2 dominated ~45% time; after bump attention_kernel_v3 + launch_overhead now ~70% and we hit a fallback kernel for masked_softmax. snippet: 
```
Kernel timings (ms):
  attention_kernel_v2  1.2
  attention_kernel_v3  2.8  <-- new slow path
  masked_softmax_fallback 0.9  <-- used for seq<64 occasionally
  kv_cache_write 0.3
```

alex.ng: Also seeing more kernel launches (x1.6) leading to scheduler contention and worse batching aggregation. Could be a driver scheduling change that makes small kernels more expensive.

sam.k: Did we change Triton or PyTorch versions at the same time? Infra said only driver+cuda minor bump but let's confirm.

maria.z: Infra notes: CUDA toolkit 12.2.1 -> 12.2.2, NVIDIA driver 535.xx -> 536.xx. No deliberate triton/pytorch change on dedicated pool.

ryan.t: I bisected in CI by rolling back driver on a single node/image; perf recovered. So it seems driver bump is correlated. But need to confirm kernel selection change origin: driver, cuBLAS, or Triton JIT codegen.

alex.ng: I also captured Triton kernel selection table from runtime: 
```
model: attn; seq=32; head=64; kernel_candidates: [attn_v3_fast, attn_v2_fused, masked_softmax_fallback]
selected: attn_v3_fast  (estimated flops higher after cuBLAS returns different heuristics)
```

maria.z: If cuBLAS or driver changed performance characteristics, our kernel selector heuristic (which uses microbenchmarks and cost model) might now prefer attn_v3 for certain shapes even if it's slower in practice for small seqs because of higher launch overhead.

sam.k: Can we quickly add a guard: prefer attn_v2 for seq<=64 as a hotfix? That would be a config toggle and avoid infra rollbacks while infra investigates.

ryan.t: I can patch runtime to bias cost model: add static penalty to attn_v3 for small-seq shapes. I'll push draft.

alex.ng: Before that, can we confirm KV cache behavior? We saw extra kv_cache_write freq in traces. Maybe cache evictions cause more small launches.

ryan.t: KV cache timings look same per op but we have more frequent partial-batches because batching heuristics break when single-request latency jumps. So feedback loop.

perf-ci: canary/deploy (dedicated-3): deploy failed health checks 2023-08-20T15:32Z, canary p50 latency +18%. Marked rollout-blocker.

maria.z: OK marking as rollout blocker. @infra can you pin the driver or roll back on dedicated-3?

alex.ng: infra already rolling a revert for one node pool to validate. But we want a software mitigation too.

sam.k: +1 to short-term runtime bias. Long term we need microbench harness in CI that runs small-seq kernels after driver upgrades.

ryan.t: Pushed runtime patch to feature/bias-attnv2-smallseq. simple diff: add heuristic tweak: 
```diff
- cost_attn_v3 = estimate_cost(shape)
+ cost_attn_v3 = estimate_cost(shape) + (shape.seq<=64 ? 0.0008 : 0)
```
Rolling it out to canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy/canary started: feature/bias-attnv2-smallseq -> canary group (2 nodes)

alex.ng: If this fixes p50 for small-seq, we can avoid infra rollback and open issue with NVIDIA with repro. We'll gather perf traces and file a bug.

perf-ci: canary results: p50 small-batch back to baseline within 5% after bias patch. End-to-end: PASS for canary group.

maria.z: Great. Merge the patch with tests + add a nightly microbench for seq {16,32,64} on driver change runs.

ryan.t: Will open PR and add a CI job. Also capturing nvprof traces and a minimal repro to NVIDIA: 
```text
Repro: CUDA 12.2.2, driver 536.x, model=redwood/base-1.4b, seq=32, bs=4, pytorch 2.2.0, triton 1.1.3, exact command attached. Observed attn kernel selection delta vs 12.2.1.
```

sam.k: Thanks team. Filing rollout-blocker postmortem and tagging infra/NVIDIA.

alex.ng: closing loop: infra rolled driver on one pool back; canary runtime bias landed; monitoring. Follow-up: add microbench CI + file vendor bug.
